races.paceDynamic: Knockiel Synge, Keep On Dreaming and Grange Soldier will ensure a strong gallop from the start over this stamina-sapping 3m4f trip. The veteran Knockiel Synge loves to bowl along in front here, while Keep On Dreaming showed early pace at Tipperary and Grange Soldier typically races prominently before fading. This sustained tempo over testing ground will stretch the field and expose stamina limitations. The relentless pace strongly favours hold-up horses with proven staying power who can pick up the pieces when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the three confirmed front-runners maintain their typical aggressive approach from flag-fall
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will stretch this modest field and expose stamina weaknesses, allowing patient horses to sweep past tired leaders in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Knockiel Synge uses his course experience to dictate a more measured pace early
scenarios.body: The 12-year-old can conserve energy for a telling kick, using his proven course form and tactical awareness to repel late challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Control
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses with front-runners going too slow or making errors
scenarios.body: Turnupdevolume can use his course-and-distance second from 2023 to track the leaders and pounce when they falter over the unique obstacles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Eliminates Field
scenarios.trigger: If the combination of distance, ground conditions and obstacles proves too demanding
scenarios.body: Multiple horses will fail to complete, leaving a depleted finish where any horse staying on strongly can claim victory regardless of ability.

races.paceDynamic: Laughing John is the sole committed front-runner and will set a manageable gallop without pressure early. Behind him, 11 runners including Judicial Deference, Daylatedollarshort, San Hilario, and Onlymammycanloveme will create a bottleneck in the prominent positions, leading to inevitable traffic problems turning for home. The hold-up horses like Matt Connor, Union Park, and Moab will benefit from the early steady pace but face the challenge of weaving through tiring horses. This race shape strongly favours the patient hold-up brigade who can stay out of trouble and finish fastest when others tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Laughing John sets a steady pace and the prominent group gets in each other's way
scenarios.body: The patient finishers get the perfect setup with a solid gallop to aim at and tiring horses ahead to pick off. Matt Connor and Union Park can unleash their finishing kicks when it matters most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front division stays strong
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely solid and the prominent horses maintain their positions
scenarios.body: Laughing John's sustainable speed combines with the class of Judicial Deference and Daylatedollarshort to hold off late challengers. The leaders have enough left in the tank to resist the closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-race pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Laughing John goes too slow and the field bunches up approaching the final turn
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the handiest horses in good positions prosper over stamina. Onlymammycanloveme and Powerful can quicken best from their prominent berths when the race explodes.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical mess unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners try to improve position simultaneously causing major interference
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery where positioning luck trumps ability, favouring horses drawn away from trouble. Outsiders like Fairlander and Another High Five can capitalize on the chaos ahead.

runners_data.comment: Dual-purpose, won at this meeting last year under Bowen, Flat win latest, can't discount
runners_data.spotlight: Dual-purpose; 2-8 over hurdles, his last win coming at this meeting last year off 7lb lower; no impact over timber since but won on the Flat at Bellewstown 17 days ago and Sean Bowen was on board for that win here last season; can't discount.

runners_data.name: Kalix Delabarriere
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won impressively last time but 9lb rise and overall profile raises questions
runners_data.comment: Back to form with a bang at Fairyhouse under this rider latest, obvious chance with repeat
runners_data.spotlight: Back to form with a bang at Fairyhouse under this rider latest, winning by 5l with a few of these behind; a 9lb rise for that seems fair but overall profile suggests he's far from guaranteed to back that up; obvious chance if he does.

runners_data.name: Arch Empire
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 178-day break with poor recent form over hurdles
runners_data.comment: 1-10 over hurdles, well beaten when last seen in November, others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Dual-purpose; 1-10 over hurdles; soundly beaten off 2lb higher when last seen at Down Royal in November; others make more appeal.

runners_data.name: Larzac
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing better effort on handicap debut last time but 1lb wrong at the weights
runners_data.comment: Improved effort on h'cap bow latest, this shorter trip a plus, 1lb wrong but a player
runners_data.spotlight: Better effort on handicap debut at Cork (2m3f, yielding) on latest, travelling strongly before weakening in the closing stages; 1lb wrong here but it's early days and this shorter trip should suit; player.

runners_data.name: Autumn Twist
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with dual-purpose background but pulled up at 40-1 last time at Cork
runners_data.comment: Maiden and novice hurdle winner, yet to fire in h'caps, pulled up latest, others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Dual-purpose; maiden and novice hurdle winner has yet to fire in handicaps; pulled up when 40-1 at Cork on latest; others hold more pressing claims.

races.paceDynamic: Touch Me Not, Full Of Life, and Jet To Monte Carlo will ensure a strong gallop from the flag with all three confirmed front-runners likely to commit early. This sustained pace over 2m½f on yielding ground will create a stamina test, particularly as Full Of Life has shown she can make all in Grade company and Touch Me Not has natural pace. The relentless tempo will set up the race for hold-up horses with tactical speed to pick off tired leaders, while prominent racers with stamina will also benefit. This race shape strongly favours hold-up performers and stamina-laden types who can finish strongly off a searching gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders maintain a genuine gallop throughout and weaken inside the final half-mile
scenarios.body: The strong pace will soften up the front-runners, allowing patient hold-up horses with tactical speed to sweep past tired leaders in the closing stages. Karbau and I'm Slippy can benefit from their proven ability to finish strongly off strong paces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers can track the pace without over-racing and maintain stamina reserves
scenarios.body: Khrisma or We're Red And Blue can position perfectly behind the leaders and have enough left to strike when the pace-setters weaken. Their tactical positioning allows them to benefit from the strong gallop while avoiding the early pace battle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Test
scenarios.trigger: If Touch Me Not or Full Of Life can dictate at a more measured tempo than expected
scenarios.body: One of the leaders manages the pace better than rivals anticipate and has enough stamina reserves to repel late challengers. Full Of Life's Grade 3 winning form suggests she can sustain a gallop over this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders go too fast early and all three crack before the final furlong
scenarios.body: The early pace battle becomes unsustainable, leaving the race at the mercy of horses that settled further back but lack the tactical speed to capitalize. This scenario opens the door for unconsidered hold-up horses who rarely win but benefit from chaos.

watchPoints.text: Touch Me Not and Full Of Life both returning from breaks of 47-48 days which could compromise their fitness for this stamina test
Karbau stopped quickly when beaten at Fairyhouse last time according to jockey report despite being favourite
Khrisma represents in-form Henderson yard making rare Irish raid but pulled up after bad mistake last time
Mode Avion faces a 14lb higher mark than his easy handicap debut win just three weeks ago
Several Mullins runners including Karbau, Murcia, and Kalix Delabarriere give the champion trainer multiple chances

races.name: PRL Champion Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)

runners_data.name: Skylight Hustle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form but 48 days off could blunt his edge against these classy rivals
runners_data.comment: Point, maiden hurdle and Gr' 1 winner, trip too far on latest, could rebound; hooded
runners_data.spotlight: One of three for stable; point winner; beaten in sole bumper and on hurdles debut at Gowran in early November; off the mark in a maiden at Fairyhouse later that month and took the step up to Grade 1 company in his stride at Leopardstown's Christmas meeting, winning by 5l; beaten when falling in the 2m5f Turners at Cheltenham; this trip more suitable and could bounce back in the first time hood.

runners_data.name: El Cairos
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with smart bumper form and a fall last time out shows he can win when getting a clear round
runners_data.comment: Didn't get home in the Supreme, this track more suitable, big chance if jumps well
runners_data.spotlight: One of three for yard; smart bumper form; fell with race at his mercy on hurdles debut at Leopardstown in December; survived a final flight blunder to win a maiden at Thurles; didn't get home up the Cheltenham hill in the Supreme last time; this track should suit better; preferred by Kennedy and big chance if cutting out the jumping errors.

runners_data.name: Sober
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up runner whose Flat class gives him a potent finishing kick but the shorter trip may not suit
runners_data.comment: Classy on Flat, C&D Grade 2 winner, poor latest but could rebound, preferred by Townend
runners_data.spotlight: One of three for yard; Group 2 winner on the Flat for Andre Fabre and won the Queen Alexandra for this stable at Ascot; bright start over hurdles, winning a 2m4f Killarney novice (yielding) and a Grade 2 novice over this C&D (sft-hvy); jumped poorly and well beaten stepped up to Grade 1 company in the Turners at Cheltenham; capable of better than that and notable that he is the choice of Townend.

runners_data.name: Free Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent type making his graded debut after disappointing Irish bow, needs to show much more
runners_data.comment: French winner, has come up short on first two runs for Willie Mullins, more needed
runners_data.spotlight: One of three for yard; French recruit; won on second start for Daniela Mele at Dieppe (2m1f, soft); last of three over C&D in Grade 2 on Irish debut; never involved when 100-1 in the Supreme last time; major improvement required.

runners_data.name: Eachtotheirown
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose two wins came from the lead but graded company looks a big step up
runners_data.comment: Has come up well short in two previous runs in graded races, hood goes on
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins have come when ridden from the front, a Galway maiden hurdle and a Thurles handicap off 124; has come up well short in both previous runs in graded company; now tried in a hood; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Blake
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with impressive hurdles debut win but fell last time and only 23 days since that tumble
runners_data.comment: Closely matched with Koktail Brut and Le Labo, go close with clear round of jumping
runners_data.spotlight: Flat winner; won impressively on hurdles debut at Down Royal and then touched off in the Royal Bond by Koktail Brut; further behind that rival in DRF Grade 1 and beaten a neck by Le Labo in Grade 3 at Naas; still in the mix when falling at the last at Fairyhouse last time in first-time cheekpieces (discarded); can go close with a clear round.

runners_data.name: Koktail Brut
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who beat Blake in Royal Bond but looked exposed in Grade 1 company at Leopardstown
runners_data.comment: Dual Grade 2 winner, closely matched with Blake, drying track would be a slight worry
runners_data.spotlight: One of three for yard; bright start over timber, winning a C&D maiden (heavy) and beating Blake by a head in the Royal Bond; limitations seemingly exposed in Grade 1 company on his next three runs but back on song with a Grade 2 win at Fairyhouse last time (left in lead after Blake fell at the last); wouldn't want the track to dry out too much.

runners_data.name: Too Bossy For Us
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with useful Flat form but Supreme flop suggests this grade may be beyond him
runners_data.comment: Useful on Flat, struggled up in class since C&D maiden win, overlooked by Townend
runners_data.spotlight: One of three for yard; Useful on the Flat; off the mark over hurdles in a C&D maiden in February (sft-hvy); beaten 11.5l when midfield in the Supreme at Cheltenham (when Townend rode) and raced keenly before pulled up in the Fairyhouse Grade 2 won by Koktail Brut latest; overlooked by Townend here.

runners_data.name: Le Labo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with mishaps over hurdles including a fall when well-placed, needs a clear round to show ability
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete first two starts over timber, beat Blake in Gr'3 latest, go well again
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner; mishaps first two runs over timber, unseating at the first at Thurles then falling with the race at his mercy at Cork; put in a clear round last time in a Grade 3 at Naas (16.5f, sft-hvy) and lowered the colours of Blake by a neck; should go well again if as effective on this quicker ground (bumper win on good).

races.paceDynamic: Eachtotheirown will lead from the gates with no other natural front-runners in this field, allowing Barry Connell's charge to dictate terms at a comfortable gallop. The prominent runners Skylight Hustle, Free Spirit and Too Bossy For Us will track the leader in the early stages, while the hold-up brigade of El Cairos, Sober, Blake, Koktail Brut and Le Labo will be held up towards the rear. With only one pace-setter and soft ground conditions, this sets up as a tactical affair that will develop into a sprint from the final flight. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can produce their best turn of foot late in the piece.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Eachtotheirown sets modest fractions and the race becomes a sprint from the last
scenarios.body: The patient tactics allow the class horses to unleash their finishing kicks when it matters most. El Cairos, Sober, Blake and Koktail Brut all have the speed and class to capitalise on this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent trackers strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens approaching the home turn and the hold-up horses get caught flat-footed
scenarios.body: Skylight Hustle and Too Bossy For Us are perfectly placed to capitalise when the tempo lifts. Their forward positions allow them to kick clear before the back-markers can respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner stays brave
scenarios.trigger: If Eachtotheirown maintains his gallop to the line and the pursuers fail to catch him
scenarios.body: The yielding ground and lack of early pressure allows the leader to conserve energy for a strong finish. His previous front-running victories at Galway and Thurles prove he can make all when conditions suit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and mistakes
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make jumping errors or fall at crucial stages of the race
scenarios.body: The novice nature of this field means blunders are likely, opening up opportunities for horses who maintain fluent jumping. Blake and Le Labo have both shown vulnerability at obstacles previously.

watchPoints.text: Eachtotheirown could steal this if allowed an uncontested lead with his front-running style perfectly suited to these conditions
Blake returns quickly from a fall just 23 days ago which could affect his jumping confidence at crucial stages
Le Labo has fallen or unseated in three of his five hurdles starts, making him a risky proposition despite his ability
El Cairos and Koktail Brut renew rivalry after their previous encounters with the former seeking revenge for that Royal Bond defeat
The Mullins quartet of Sober, Free Spirit and Too Bossy For Us could work in tandem to set this up for one of their number

races.name: Dooley Insurance Group Champion Novice Chase (Grade 1)

runners_data.name: Kitzbuhel
runners_data.note: Class front-runner with Grade 1 form but 48 days off and faces two other pace rivals which could compromise his tactics
runners_data.comment: Best of the Mullins quartet judged on his Brown Advisory win atoning for Sandown failure
runners_data.spotlight: Set the early standard in the staying novice division, winning Grade 1 Kauto Star at Kempton (3m, good) at Christmas after a 2m3f beginners' win at this venue; blotted his record in Sandown Grade 1, jumped right before unseating at the sixth; redeemed himself with a stylish front-running victory in the Brown Advisory; now looks strongest of the Mullins quartet.

runners_data.name: Fleur In The Park
runners_data.note: Prominent racer suited by yielding ground but trainer form concerning at 6/31 over past fortnight
runners_data.comment: A revelation when winning 2m4f Grade 1 at Fairyhouse, fair chance of getting this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 2m beginners' chase at Wexford in October; went close in a 2m Grade 2 here in November; after a break, well below his best at Thurles in March; career-best with the help of new hold-up tactics when outsider of eight in Grade 1 Fairyhouse, beating Kappa Jy Pyke; third in a Grade 1 novice hurdle here a year ago; fair chance of staying this far.

runners_data.name: July Flower
runners_data.note: Hold-up merchant ideally suited by strong pace but stamina questions remain after recent 2m4f disappointment
runners_data.comment: Only mare in the field, reservations about stamina and seems short of the standard needed
runners_data.spotlight: Won Grade 2 Arkle Trial over 2m at Cheltenham in November before finishing third in 2m1f event at Leopardstown in December; appeared not to stay the extended 2m4f in the Grade 2 mares' chase at the Cheltenham Festival; however, she was placed in a Grade 1 hurdle around this distance in France two seasons ago.

runners_data.name: Oscars Brother
runners_data.note: Patient type from unfashionable yard with decent 3m form but 17-day turnaround could be insufficient recovery
runners_data.comment: Late progress to finish fourth behind Kitzbuhel at Cheltenham, unseated in Grand National
runners_data.spotlight: Prospered after second to Western Fold on chase debut at Tipperary last May; hat-trick included small-field 3m Grade 2s at this venue and Navan; took time to warm up and left with plenty to do in the Brown Advisory, made late progress to finish fourth behind Kitzbuhel; towards the back when unseated at the 15th (Chair) in the Grand National.

runners_data.name: Kappa Jy Pyke
runners_data.note: Prominent racer improving as chaser with strong same-going record at 7/7 wins and places
runners_data.comment: Failed to cope with Fleur In The Park at Fairyhouse, helps to add depth to stable's squad
runners_data.spotlight: Found wanting at Grade 1 level over hurdles last season; much more accomplished as a chaser; beat a long odds-on stablemate in Thurles beginners' event; beat Jacob's Ladder readily here in January in a Grade 3 race in which Predators Gold gave a below-par display; failed to cope with Fleur In The Park at Fairyhouse.

runners_data.name: Western Fold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent form figures but Gordon Elliott's 6/43 recent strike-rate raises questions
runners_data.comment: Needs to recapture early-season form, Galway Plate winner and Grade 2 Gowran scorer
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive in the first half of the season; won the Galway Plate, beat subsequent Savills Chase winner Affordale Fury at Gowran in October; second to Kaid d'Authie in an unsatisfactory four-runner DRF event; faded from three out in Brown Advisory; badly hampered and unseated two out in Fairyhouse Grade 1 won by Fleur In The Park.

runners_data.name: Predators Gold
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from long absence with amateur jockey potentially compromising tactical options
runners_data.comment: Going well when falling two out in the 2m4f Fairyhouse Grade 1 won by Fleur In The Park
runners_data.spotlight: Smart novice hurdler in 2023-24 season before 19-month absence; returned to win a beginners' event at Navan in December, beating Slade Steel; jumping was untidy when he was beaten at odds-on by stablemate Kappa Jy Pyke here in January; challenging and going well when falling two out in the 2m4f Fairyhouse Grade 1 won by Fleur In The Park.

runners_data.name: Lovely Hurling
runners_data.comment: Non-runner
runners_data.spotlight: Non-runner

runners_data.name: Spanish Harlem
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with handicap background but multiple recent falls create significant jumping concerns
runners_data.comment: Kerry National winner last autumn, non-finisher four times since then, very risky
runners_data.spotlight: Smart staying handicapper at his best; won the Kerry National at Listowel last September and looked set for victory in the Thyestes at Gowran Park in January when unseating at the final fence; pulled up in the Bobbyjo at Fairyhouse, same outcome in the Grand National.

runners_data.name: Nowwhatdoyouthink
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up significantly in class despite recent course win over shorter trip
runners_data.comment: Fine effort when winning a three-runner Cork event, takes a big jump in class.
runners_data.spotlight: Point, bumper and maiden hurdle winner; off the mark over fences at this track (2m5f) in November; better effort when second to C'Est Ta Chance in a Thurles novice event over a similar trip; good effort when winning a three-runner Cork event; takes a big jump in class.

races.paceDynamic: Kitzbuhel and Predators Gold will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners likely to set a solid gallop over this 3m1f trip. Their presence ensures an honest pace throughout, preventing any stop-start tactics that could disadvantage the staying types. The extended distance and yielding ground will test stamina reserves in the final half-mile, with the pace likely to fragment the field. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and prominent racers with proven stamina, as they can capitalise on the pace collapse from the early leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Kitzbuhel and Predators Gold duel early and fade late
scenarios.body: The strong early gallop will set up perfectly for closers like July Flower, Western Fold and Spanish Harlem who can pick up the pieces. Their patient tactics and stamina reserves become decisive advantages when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Kitzbuhel gets an uncontested lead and controls the tempo
scenarios.body: The class horse can dictate terms without serious pressure, saving energy for a sustained drive to the line. His Grade 1 credentials and Townend's tactical nous prove decisive in a truly-run staying test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate allowing prominent horses to stay connected
scenarios.body: Horses like Kappa Jy Pyke and Fleur In The Park can track the leaders without over-racing and strike late. Their positioning advantage and fresh conditions favour them over both leaders and hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners are pulled up or fall early in the race
scenarios.body: The field bunches up creating a sprint finish that could favour any horse with tactical speed. Form and class become less relevant as positioning and luck dominate the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Spanish Harlem has fallen in three of his last five starts and represents a clear jumping risk for others
Predators Gold showed rusty jumping on comeback at Navan and could make errors under amateur rider
Kitzbuhel needs watching if Predators Gold goes with him early as neither may want to give way
Western Fold's recent Thurles pull-up suggests possible issues despite Elliott's confidence in running
July Flower requires strong pace to be effective so watch for her position turning for home

runners_data.spotlight: E65,000 2yo, E200,000 3yo; tenth foal; half-brother by Nathaniel to winners, notably the talented Santini; dam 1m4f Flat/2m hurdle winner; could be a big player with Derek O'Connor aboard.

runners_data.spotlight: E75,000 foal, E60,000 3yo; Nathaniel gelding second foal out of Limini, a middle distance Flat winner and smart hurdle winner for Willie Mullins; family of Irish Oaks winner Vintage Tipple; strong trainer/rider combination.

runners_data.name: Sierrascope

runners_data.name: Whispered Verdict
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to two German winners, stable's Bacharach was a much more expensive purchase
runners_data.spotlight: E11,000 Y, E24,000 3yo; fourth foal; half-brother to two German winners; dam German Group 3 winner; stable's Bacharach was a much more expensive purchase.

runners_data.name: Altesse du Luy
runners_data.comment: E145,000 3yo, trainer has won this in three of the last five years, should be in the mix

runners_data.name: Barstool Prophet
runners_data.comment: E30,000 3yo, third foal; dam a bumper/chase winner by Kings Theatre; cheekpieces fitted
runners_data.spotlight: E23,000 F, E30,000 3yo; third foal; filly by Crystal Ocean out of a bumper/chase winner by Kings Theatre; cheekpieces fitted.

runners_data.name: Birdie Conway
runners_data.comment: E15,000 3yo, cheap purchase, pedigree boosted by her dam's sister The Mourne Rambler
runners_data.spotlight: E15,000 3yo; first foal; Jet Away filly out of an unraced sister to stable's Champion Bumper winner The Mourne Rambler, and two other useful performers, Sixshooter and She's A Star.

runners_data.spotlight: E38,000 F, E20,000 3yo; third foal; dam unraced sister to point winner Royal Captain; plenty of stamina in the pedigree; rider partnered the stable's 2021 winner Adamantly Chosen.

races.name: William Hill Champion Chase (Grade 1)

runners_data.name: Majborough
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with huge engine and Grade 1 class, 48 days fresh could be ideal for Willie Mullins' stable jockey choice
runners_data.comment: Three-time Grade 1 winner, erratic jumper at times, big chance if jumps well but risky
runners_data.spotlight: 4-8 over fences; has a massive engine and has won three Grade 1s over fences, including when giving Marine Nationale a 19l beating in first-time cheekpieces at the DRF; however, his jumping is often erratic and the cheekpieces weren't as effective when he again jumped poorly when soundly beaten in the Champion Chase; obvious chance if he jumps well but hard to know what to expect; a risky proposition.

runners_data.name: Energumene
runners_data.note: 12-year-old veteran with prominent style needs to prove he retains enough pace to match these younger rivals

runners_data.name: Marine Nationale
runners_data.note: Freshest of the main contenders after missing Cheltenham, prominent style suits this tactical scenario perfectly
runners_data.comment: 2025 Champion Chaser, won this last year, fresh, gets his ground, big chance
runners_data.spotlight: The 2025 Champion Chaser arrives here a fresher horse than most after missing Cheltenham with a sore neck; returned to action at Leopardstown in December with a pleasing effort behind Solness after making an early mistake; no match for Majborough at the DRF on testing ground but he's a much better horse on a sounder surface; won this in fine style last year and could repeat the dose.

runners_data.name: Blood Destiny
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner will dictate terms but needs career-best effort to resist superior-rated chasers in behind
runners_data.comment: Fourth chase win in Naas Gr'3 on penultimate, 6l behind Energumene on latest
runners_data.spotlight: One of four for Willie Mullins; gained a fourth chase win in a Naas Grade 3 in February; creditable effort when a 6l runner up behind Energumene in a Fairyhouse Grade 2 on latest; 3lb worse off with that rival here and looks set to play a supporting role again.

runners_data.name: Il Etait Temps
runners_data.note: Hold-up style puts him at tactical disadvantage in this small field where pace pressure may be limited
runners_data.comment: 8-11 over fences including six Grade 1s, bolted up in Champion Chase latest, big chance
runners_data.spotlight: Ground versatile; not the biggest in stature but a hugely talented performer who has won eight of his 11 chase starts, including six Grade 1s; bolted up in the Champion Chase on latest, immediately bouncing back from a rare blip at Sandown; won a Grade 1 novice over C&D at this meeting last year and he's preferred by Townend; leading chance.

races.paceDynamic: Blood Destiny will lead from the flag with his front-running style, setting what should be a steady tempo over this 2m½f trip without serious early pressure from the prominent racers. Majborough, Energumene, Marine Nationale and Il Etait Temps will all track within striking distance, creating a compact group behind the leader through the early stages. The pace will intensify from three out as the prominently-raced horses begin to close on Blood Destiny, setting up a sustained drive from the final fence. This tactical setup strongly favours the prominent racers who can track the pace and unleash their finishing kicks, rather than the pure front-runner or hold-up horse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Power Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent racers track Blood Destiny comfortably and kick from three out
scenarios.body: Majborough, Energumene and Marine Nationale can all utilise their class advantage over Blood Destiny when the tempo lifts approaching the business end. Their prominent style perfectly suits tracking the lone leader before asserting superiority in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny maintains a strong gallop and the chasers leave their moves too late
scenarios.body: The 7-year-old's stamina reserves could prove decisive if he can string out his pursuers over this demanding trip on yielding ground. His recent Naas Grade 3 win suggests he retains enough ability to exploit any tactical hesitation behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong and the prominent horses get drawn into battle
scenarios.body: Il Etait Temps could benefit from Paul Townend's patient tactics if the others go too hard too soon in their pursuit of Blood Destiny. His hold-up style would allow him to pick up the pieces if the pace collapses the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny sets an unsustainably fast tempo under pressure from the field
scenarios.body: A muddling, stop-start gallop could compromise all the prominent racers who rely on a true test of stamina and class. This tactical lottery scenario would favour whichever horse gets the clearest run rather than pure ability.

watchPoints.text: Blood Destiny's early fractions will determine if this becomes a staying test or speed contest for the prominent racers
Energumene's jumping under pressure at 12 years old could be the decisive factor if he gets into a battle
Marine Nationale's fitness after 86-day break may only surface in the final furlong under maximum pressure
Il Etait Temps needs the pace to collapse to get competitive from his hold-up position in this tactical setup
Majborough's response to first-time headgear removal could indicate Willie Mullins' confidence levels
